context: The input is a 4×4 grid of nonnegative integer costs, grid, with zero-based indices (see the input table for all values). Go from the top-left cell [0,0] to the bottom-right cell [3,3], moving one cell right or down at each step. Include the values of both endpoints in the total.
In the state table, dp[i,j] is the minimum path sum from [0,0] to row i, column j. Each initial 0 is a placeholder for an uncomputed value. It does not indicate a path of cost 0.
description: Initialize the boundary starting with dp[0,0] = grid[0,0] = 1. Row 0 can only be reached by moving right, and column 0 only by moving down. Accumulating costs along these paths gives values for all 7 boundary cells.

For the 9 interior cells in rows 1–3 and columns 1–3, process each row from left to right using dp[i,j] = min(dp[i-1,j], dp[i,j-1]) + grid[i,j]. This ensures the values above (dp[i-1,j]) and to the left (dp[i,j-1]) are ready. In each frame, the state table labels each value as an uncomputed initial value, a valid boundary value, or a computed value so you can look it up by coordinate.

summary: Start at the top left and accumulate the costs along the only paths through the first row and first column. Then work row by row to the bottom right, adding each cell's cost to the smaller of the totals above and to the left.
